newsitem.title: GERMANY: German SPD says tax gaps show govt policy unreal.
newsitem.headline: German SPD says tax gaps show govt policy unreal.

text.p: Oskar Lafontaine, leader of the opposition Social Democrats (SPD), said on Thursday that large shortfalls in tax revenue show that Chancellor Helmut Kohl's tax policies are unrealistic.

"The current fiscal crisis is the result of the wrong economic and financial policies of the Kohl government, which are driving Germany ever deeper into unemployment," Lafontaine said. "The huge budget gaps show that Kohl's tax plans are completely unrealistic."

The government and SPD abandoned attempts to reach a cross-party consensus earlier this year on a comprehensive tax reform proposed by Finance Minister Theo Waigel, due to differences over cutting the top income tax rate and other fine points.
"We challenge the government to make way for a solid tax reform," Lafontaine said.
The stated aim of Waigel's was to boost investment and jobs, as Germany struggles to reduce unemployment from postwar record levels seen over the winter.
